Officer's narrative
Officer's narrative. On arrival at the scene in Baytown, Texas, I found two vehicles in a low-speed head-on collision in
the eastbound lane. Driver 1 was seated behind the wheel of the first vehicle and reported pain in the right shoulder
fololwing the impact. Driver 2 stated that their vehicle crossed the centerline during a lane change and struck the front
of Driver 1's vehicle. Driver 2 was able to explain the sequence clearly and did not contradict the account given by
Driver 1. Two witnesses on the roadside independently described the same sequence, and photographs taken at the
scene show damage to both front ends that is consistent with the impact described. Dirver 1 is listed as the named
insured on the policy for the vehicle involved. Passenger was seated in the front passenger seat of the same vehicle,
though the exact seating position at the moment of impact was not fully clear from the statements taken. No prior
damage to either vehicle was observed or reported. Whether the shoulder injury resulted from this colliison has not
yet been determined and will require medical follow-up. Both drivers were cooperative, and no citations were issued
at the scene.
</page>
